FN-G3YLI62-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 252
Committee: Banking and Insurance Sponsor: Senator Billy Beasley
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/19/2025
Senate Bill 252 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Department of Insurance by
providing further for the regulation and enforcement of pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs)
operating within the state, by requiring the Commissioner to adopt additional rules pursuant to
the provisions of this bill and to set and impose civil penalties not less than $1,000 per violation
of this bill and the Pharmacy Audit Integrity Act. This bill could also increase receipts to the
State General Fund by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of and amount of civil
penalties (not less than $1,000 per violation) imposed by the Commissioner for violating the
provisions of this bill.
In addition, due to the changes in the estimated costs of utilizing pharmacy benefits managers
pursuant to the provisions of this bill, this bill would increase the obligations of the Local
Government Health Insurance Plan (LGHIP) by an undetermined amount and per the Alabama
State Employees Insurance Board, increase the costs of the State Employees' Health Insurance
Plan (SEHIP) by an estimated $4.1 million annually.

FN-G3YLI62-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 252
Committee: Insurance Sponsor: Senator Billy Beasley
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 04/01/2025
Senate Bill 252 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of the
Department of Insurance by providing further for the regulation and enforcement of pharmacy
benefit managers (PBMs) operating within the state, by requiring the Commissioner to adopt
additional rules pursuant to the provisions of this bill. This bill could also increase receipts to
the Insurance Department Fund by up to $100 for each complaint filing fee paid by a pharmacy
or pharmacist alleging certain violations and which shall be repaid to the complainant by a PBM
found in violation. This bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund by an
undetermined amount dependent on the amount of civil penalties, not less than $1,000 per
violation, imposed by the Commissioner for violating the provisions of this bill.
In addition, this bill would increase the obligations of: (1) the Local Government Health
Insurance Plan (LGHIP) by an undetermined amount dependent on the change in costs of
utilizing pharmacy benefits managers pursuant to the provisions of this bill; and (2) the Alabama
State Employees Insurance Board, for the State Employees' Health Insurance Plan (SEHIP) by a
board-estimated $4.1 million annually.
